rulings.restated: Add person.one over every confirmed person entry for which (helper "Do you have an SSN valid for employment issued before the due date of your return?" = true or helper "Do you have an SSN or ITIN issued on or before the due date of your return, or have you applied for an ITIN by then?" = true), within the current person when parent-bound. An unanswered roster is unknown.
rulings.model: The second test counts someone who has only applied for an ITIN. For the spouse without a valid SSN, the IRS text says "The other spouse must have either an SSN or ITIN, and it must have been issued on or before the due date of the return".
rulings.ruling: Ruling: second transcription right; data fixed. For the child tax credit 'The other spouse must have either an SSN or ITIN, and it must have been issued on or before the due date of the return' (i1040gi p. 17, Before you begin); the count now reads person.tin, which asks only for an issued number, and no longer an application for an ITIN (person.itin_applied). BUG-0049.

rulings.restated: Add dependent.one over every confirmed dependent entry for which helper "A Test 2 person who lived with you more than half the year (the home-cost condition of Test 2 is tested on the household form)" = true, within the current person when parent-bound. An unanswered roster is unknown.
rulings.model: Test 2 also counts persons who are not your dependents: 'Your unmarried qualifying child who isn't your dependent' and items 3 and 4. The restatement counts only 'confirmed dependent entries', and the text given does not say whether the roster includes these non-dependent qualifying children. The per-person helper's handling of the 'Exception to time lived with you' and the exclusions a–c is also not shown.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. "Confirmed entry" is the renderer's wording for every person listed, not for dependents only; `dependent.hoh_test2` counts a claimed dependent who lived with the filer more than half the year and is not a household-member-only dependent, or an unmarried qualifying child who lived with the filer more than half the year whether or not a dependent (i1040gi p. 14, Test 2, items 1 and 2). Items 3 and 4 and exclusions (a) and (c) are the divorced-parent and multiple-support rules, which are refused. No change to the data.

rulings.restated: Add person.one over every confirmed person entry for which helper "Do you have an SSN or ITIN issued on or before the due date of your return, or have you applied for an ITIN by then?" = true, within the current person when parent-bound. An unanswered roster is unknown.
rulings.model: The per-person test counts someone who has only applied for an ITIN by the due date. For you and your spouse, the IRS text requires an issued number: "you, and your spouse if filing jointly, must have either an SSN or ITIN issued on or before the due date of your 2025 return". The "applying for an ITIN" allowance appears only for the child, in Step 3.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: project retained; the question is now split. Step 5, question 1 (the credit for other dependents) asks whether you, and your spouse if filing jointly, have an SSN or ITIN issued on or before the due date and adds '(Answer "Yes" if you are applying for an ITIN on or before the return due date (including extensions).)' (i1040gi p. 19). person.tin now asks only for an issued number and person.itin_applied for an application; this count, for the credit for other dependents, accepts either.
